their_var: Cost of forest residues (feedstock supply cost at refinery)
evidence_quote: The cost of forest residues varies widely, ranging from $20 to $80 per tonne. This can cause the SAF production cost to increase from $1.41 per kg to $2.27 per kg.
note: Range $20-80/tonne and $1.41-2.27/kg effect verbatim; feedstock cost is a perturbed SA input.

evidence_quote: if inflation increases up to 4%, it can increase the unit production cost to $1.93 per kg.
note: Plausible perturbed SA input; quote verbatim.

evidence_quote: When steam usage is increased by 20% to 0.42 kg kg-1, the GW impact increases to 42.7 gCO2 eq. per kg of SAF, whereas a 20% reduction in steam usage decreases the GW impact to 6 gCO2 eq.
note: Plausible perturbed SA input; quote verbatim.

their_var: Electricity usage (kW h per kg SAF)
evidence_quote: increasing electricity usage by 20% to 0.154 kW h kg results in a GWP impact of 41.9 gCO2 eq. per kg, while a 20% decrease reduces it to 6.89 gCO2 eq. per kg.
note: Plausible perturbed SA input; quote verbatim.

evidence_quote: a decrease in Fischer-Tropsch conversion efficiency to 80% from 100% shows an increase in GWP to 32.7 gCO2 eq. per kg of SAF.
note: Plausible perturbed SA input; quote verbatim.

evidence_quote: Variations in forest residue requirements by +/-20% lead to GWP values ranging from 23.8 to 25.3 gCO2 eq. per kg of SAF.
note: Plausible perturbed SA input; quote verbatim.

evidence_quote: changes in diethanolamine requirements for gas treatment show a minor impact on GWI, varying from 24.4 to 24.8 gCO2 eq. per kg of SAF.
note: Plausible perturbed SA input; quote verbatim.
